svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: Task-grounded paired evaluation. The same participant-safe task and benchmark-owned concurrent initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. A, B and C are illustrative independent subagents, not a fixed model pool or a required count. Private event rules cover eight benchmark event themes and define affected work and work to keep without exposing scoring truth. Linear waits for all terminal child states and then shows one stable result batch to the main agent. In Async, Main, A, B and C share a qualitative horizontal time axis. Main begins after the initial worker start and keeps working across C completion. C finishes at an earlier schematic instant than actual main presentation. C results pass through public submission checking, event send rules, sending, waiting and inclusion in a launched main-model request. Identical amber lightning ports link that actual presentation to the later start of the purple handling segment; they are a symbolic continuation, not a bypass or a continuous drawn edge. Main resumes blue ongoing work after handling; A and B run throughout completion, presentation and handling and continue beyond the displayed fragment. A short control arrow illustrates a later adjustment to still-running A. Time has no units and is not measured or to scale. No event cancels an in-flight API request. Updating and keeping valid work may happen together. Run records capture actual delivery, presentation, agent actions and event-boundary artifact digests; hidden scoring checks do not suppress public delivery. BTS arrows represent eventual final states of the whole routes, not completion of the displayed time fragment. DRS uses independent event and state evidence, half process and half event outcome, without strict attribution to one response window. Metrics aggregate independently through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight event-theme means, with coverage reported separately.
